approval.cost: No review or listing fee is stated anywhere in the docs read (publishing a listed app auto-enrolls you in the App Partner Program)
approval.trigger: Review is mandatory for ALL public apps: 'In order to make your app public and available for customers to install, you will need to submit it for a review from the Intercom team.' 'Both unlisted and listed apps must be submitted for review.' Private apps are exempt ('Private apps that only access your own paid workspace data do not require a review'). Pre-approval, the cap is categorical: 'During this process, your app will be private and can only be used by you and your team.' On approval 'it will become a public unlisted app' (you then opt in to App Store listing separately via 'List in App store'). Submission happens in the Developer Hub's Test and publish section: complete the App Partner Program information (and, if listing, the App Store listing and Start guide), then on the 'Submit for a review' page add the app description (including test-account credentials or setup instructions if your service needs an account) and the mandatory end-to-end video, and click Submit for Review. The video must show installation with OAuth working, the end-to-end experience, and uninstallation, and 'Please show the full client_id and state parameter in the OAuth URL'. Scope discipline is enforced: 'If you have requested scopes outside of the current functionality, you may be asked to adjust your scopes and resubmit the app'. Feedback arrives via an in-app Messenger conversation. Updates to an approved app need re-approval (the current version stays public while updates are reviewed).
approval.wait: 'It can take up to seven business days for review' (stated, including for resubmissions)

blockers.detail: Unlike marketplaces where review only gates the storefront, an unapproved Intercom public app cannot be installed by customers at all, listed or unlisted. Plan launch timing around the up-to-seven-business-day review plus possible resubmission cycles (an incomplete video alone means 'you will have to resubmit your video').
blockers.howToClear: Submit early with a complete end-to-end video and a reviewer test account ready.
blockers.title: Review gates connectivity, not just listing

blockers.detail: Workspaces live in US/EU/AU regions, each with its own /oauth host (app.intercom.com, app.eu.intercom.com, app.au.intercom.com). Using the US host for an EU/AU customer adds a region-selection step on sign-in, and 'if the customer signs in with Google, the wrong regional host fails rather than prompting, so matching the region is required in that case'.
blockers.howToClear: Detect or ask the customer's region and route to the matching authorize host.
blockers.title: Regional authorization hosts

blockers.detail: 'The code value in the redirect URL may contain a = at the end which needs to be included.' Dropping it yields a 401 with error message 'Unauthorized Code' at token exchange.
blockers.howToClear: Pass the code through to the token exchange byte-for-byte; never trim trailing characters.
blockers.title: The trailing '=' code trap

alternatives: Private app with the app's Access Token (available 'as soon as you create an app on your workspace' under Configure > Authentication; only for accessing YOUR OWN workspace data; 'do not require a review'; NOT a customer-connection mechanism)
flavor.recommended: A public app in the Intercom Developer Hub with OAuth enabled ('Use OAuth' on the Authentication page)
flavor.why: Intercom is explicit: 'If you are building a public integration that will have access to other peoples' Intercom data you are required to set up OAuth', including if 'You currently ask people for their API Keys'. Asking users for their Access Tokens instead 'is against our terms of service and may result in your API access being revoked'. Distribution flavors are Listed (discoverable in the App Store) vs Unlisted ('available for anyone to install but is not listed in the App Store: It must be installed via your own product or website'), and both are public apps requiring review. Client ID and Client Secret are on the app's Basic Information page.

humanMust: Create a development workspace and the app in the Developer Hub; tick 'Use OAuth' and add Redirect URL(s) (HTTPS required)
Select permissions (scopes) by checkbox, requesting only what you need (they 'will go up for review')
Retrieve the client_id and client_secret from the Basic Information page
Record the mandatory end-to-end review video and submit for review with a test account for Intercom's team
name: Intercom
nuances: No refresh token appears in the documented exchange: the token response documented is only token_type ('Always Bearer'), token, and access_token (a duplicate). The docs read describe no refresh grant, so design your connect UX so re-authorization is painless.

If your app uses Canvas Kit, 'Read and list users and companies', 'Read conversations', 'Read admins', and 'Gather App data' 'will be automatically selected and cannot be deselected', and reviewers will see them in your scope set.

Scope changes are review events: because scopes 'go up for review' and post-approval changes need re-approval, adding a permission later is a release-process decision. Intercom recommends keeping a separate staging app (name the twin with [Staging]/[Dev] appended).

Listed-app requirements that cause rejections: icon 512x512 PNG; app name 40 characters or less, unique, and it 'Must not contain Intercom' (names containing 'Intercom' 'will not be approved'); short description 70 characters or less; Terms of service and Privacy policy URLs; a pricing-model selection (a paid app must give a pricing-page URL or a sales contact route); Documentation URL; Support email; 'Your listing must have 2-5 images' of at least 1600x1000 PNG under 21MB; the Installation status section is mandatory and 'Providing broken or unclear links will result in an application rejection'.
Webhook topics are tied to matching scopes (e.g. a user-created webhook needs 'Read and write users').
prerequisites: A development workspace in the Intercom Developer Hub
A reviewer-ready test account for your own service if it requires one, and the end-to-end video assets

steps.detail: Developer Hub > New app > name > workspace > Create app. 'Each development workspace automatically gives you the option to use OAuth.'
steps.title: Create the app in the Developer Hub

steps.detail: On the app's Authentication page, tick 'Use OAuth'. Add Redirect URL(s) ('Redirect URLs must use HTTPS'; multiple allowed via Add redirect URL; the first is the default). Select permissions by checkbox: 'You should only specify the scopes you definitely need for your use case', because they will go up for review. Retrieve client_id and client_secret from the Basic Information page.
steps.title: Enable OAuth; add redirect URLs; select permissions

steps.detail: Send the user to the REGIONAL authorize URL: app.intercom.com/oauth (US), app.eu.intercom.com/oauth (EU), app.au.intercom.com/oauth (Australia), with client_id and state ('A random session specific string which we will return in the callback... to mitigate CSRF attacks'). The user sees the requested permissions and approves.
steps.title: Send the user to the regional authorize URL

steps.detail: Intercom redirects to your Redirect URL with code and state. POST api.intercom.io/auth/eagle/token with code, client_id, client_secret. Response: token_type ('Always Bearer'), token, and access_token (a duplicate). Call the API with Authorization: Bearer (e.g. GET api.intercom.io/me). Preserve the code exactly, including any trailing '='.
steps.title: Exchange the code; call the API

steps.detail: In the Developer Hub's Test and publish section, complete the App Partner Program information (plus the App Store listing and Start guide if listing). On the 'Submit for a review' page, add the app description (with test-account credentials or setup instructions if needed) and the mandatory end-to-end video showing installation with OAuth working, the full experience, and uninstallation, including the full client_id and state parameter in the OAuth URL. Click Submit for Review. Review can take up to seven business days.
steps.title: Submit for review (required before any customer install)

tagline: Standard authorization-code OAuth whose review gates the app itself: listed or unlisted, no external customer can install until Intercom approves (up to seven business days, with a mandatory end-to-end video), and the docs describe no refresh token at all.

time.active: ~20 min of Developer Hub setup + ~1 hr of flow code
time.total: About a week or more: review 'can take up to seven business days' (stated), plus any resubmission cycles
time.waiting: Review: up to seven business days (stated)
